BMP9 is activated by receptor-mediated displacement of its pro-domains.
the pro-domains of bone morphogenic proteins 9 are displaced upon binding of the growth factor to its receptor, thus enabling the mature growth factor to interact with the receptor.
BMP9 is activated upon binding to its receptors by non-covalent displacement of the pro-domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of an ELISA for the quantification of BMP9 protein levels in human serum.
the regulation of the bioactivity of BMP9 and provides new insight into the activation mechanism of the BMP9 signaling complex.
the activation of the bone morphogenic protein (BMP) 9 pro-domain complex by the type I and II receptor complex and the co-receptor endoglins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BMP9 is activated upon binding to the receptor and the pro-domains are displaced by the receptor.
the pro-domains of BMP9 are not inhibitory, but rather serve as a reservoir for the growth factor, which can rapidly become available for binding to the receptor upon contact.
the BMP9 pro-domain is a regulatory component that is removed from the BMP9 complex upon receptor binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pro-domain displacement from BMP9·pro-domains complexes is a rapid and efficient mechanism to activate the growth factor.
BMP9 activation is a very rapid and efficient process that does not require any additional cofactors.
the pro-domains of BMP9 do not inhibit BMP9 activity, but rather act as a storage and release device for the mature growth factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pro-domain binding by ALK1 or antibodies leads to immediate dissociation of pro-domains from pro-BMP9.
BMP9 is activated by the displacement of its pro-domains from its complex by the receptor or antibodies, and that the pro-domain-free mature BMP9 growth factors can then bind to the receptor.
the BMP9 pro-domains are not inhibitors of the growth factor but rather serve as a means to regulate the availability and bioactivity of mature growth factor.
